The last night of Elias Harrow's long career began like all the others. As the sun sank below the horizon, painting the sea in shades of amber and violet, he climbed the ninety-two steps to the lantern room, his weathered hand sliding along the cold iron railing. He had made this climb nearly twenty thousand times, and still his knees remembered every step.

Tomorrow, a new automated system would take over. There would be no need for a keeper, no need for the quiet ritual of winding the clockwork or polishing the great glass lens. The mainland officials had been kind about it, thanking him for his years of faithful service, but their words felt hollow against the roar of the waves below.

He lit the lamp and watched the beam sweep across the darkening water, steady and sure. Somewhere out there, a ship was counting on that light. Elias smiled to himself. Whatever came next, tonight the light would shine, and it would shine because of him.
